title: Phrasal verbs 7: up (1)
subtitle: come up to / set up / give up
summary: Learn phrasal verbs with up that mean approaching, starting, growing, tidying and finishing something.

lesson.heading: come up to, catch up, keep up
lesson.text: **go/come/walk up to somebody** = approach them. **catch up (with somebody)** = move faster so that you reach the people in front of you. **keep up (with somebody)** = continue at the same speed or level.

examples.text: A man **came up to** me in the street and asked me for money.
I'm not ready to go yet. You go on and I'll **catch up with** you.
You're walking too fast. I can't **keep up** (with you).
You're doing well. **Keep it up!**

lesson.heading: set up, take up, fix up
lesson.text: **set up** an organisation, a company, a system or a website = start it. **take up** a hobby, a sport or an activity = start doing it. **fix up** a meeting = arrange it.

examples.text: The government has **set up** a committee to investigate the problem.
Laura **took up** photography a few years ago. She takes really good pictures.
We've **fixed up** a meeting for next Monday.

lesson.heading: grow up and bring up
lesson.text: **grow up** = become an adult. **bring up a child** = raise a child, look after a child.

examples.text: Amy was born in Hong Kong but **grew up** in Australia.
Her parents died when she was a child and she **was brought up** by her grandparents.

lesson.heading: clean up, tidy up, wash up
lesson.text: **clean up**, **clear up** and **tidy up** = make something clean or tidy. **wash up** = wash the plates and dishes after a meal.

examples.text: Look at this mess! Who's going to **tidy up**?
I hate **washing up**.
examples.note: or I hate doing the washing-up.

lesson.heading: end up and give up
lesson.text: **end up** somewhere or **end up doing** something = that is what happens to you in the end. **give up** = stop trying; **give something up** = stop doing it.

examples.text: There was a fight in the street and three men **ended up** in hospital.
I couldn't find a hotel and **ended up sleeping** on a bench at the station.
Don't **give up**. Keep trying!
Sue got bored with her job and decided to **give it up**.

lesson.heading: make up, take up, turn up, use up
lesson.text: **make up** something or **be made up of** something = form the whole of it. **take up** space or time = use it. **turn up** or **show up** = arrive, appear. **use something up** = use all of it so that nothing is left.

examples.text: Children under 16 **make up** half the population of the city.
Air **is made up** mainly **of** nitrogen and oxygen.
Most of the space in the room **was taken up** by a large table.
We arranged to meet David last night, but he didn't **turn up**.
I'm going to make soup. We have a lot of vegetables and I want to **use them up**.

lesson.text: *take up* has two meanings: start an activity (she took up tennis) and fill space or time (the table takes up half the room).

exercises.prompt: Kate ___ the front door of the house and rang the doorbell.
exercises.explanation: go/walk up to something = approach it.

exercises.prompt: Tom was a long way behind the other runners, but he managed to ___ them.
exercises.explanation: catch up with somebody = go faster and reach the people ahead of you.

exercises.prompt: Tanya was running too fast for Paul. He couldn't ___ her.
exercises.explanation: keep up with somebody = continue at the same speed as them.

exercises.prompt: I'm feeling very tired now. I've ___ all my energy.
exercises.explanation: use something up = use all of it so that nothing is left.

exercises.prompt: People often ask children what they want to be when they ___.
We arranged to meet Tom, but he didn't ___.
exercises.explanation: turn up (or show up) = arrive, appear.

exercises.prompt: I don't do any sports right now, but I'm thinking of ___ tennis.
exercises.explanation: take up a sport or hobby = start doing it.

exercises.prompt: Karen travelled a lot for a few years and ___ in Canada, where she still lives.
exercises.explanation: end up somewhere = that is where you are in the end.

exercises.prompt: Steven is having problems at school. He can't ___ the rest of the class.
exercises.explanation: keep up with somebody = stay at the same level as them.

exercises.prompt: Helen has her own website. A friend of hers helped her to ___.
exercises.explanation: set something up = start it or get it working.

exercises.statement: Air is made up mainly of nitrogen and oxygen.
exercises.explanation: Correct. be made up of something = consist of it.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.

look after a child until they are an adult
